clauses.current_legal_basis: Held original text of EO 11139 as amended by section 68 of EO 13286 (effective March 1, 2003), read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog through 2026-10-14; no revocation, supersession or further amendment found.
clauses.reason: The sole paragraph authorizes the Secretary of Defense and, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of the Treasury to prescribe regulations for acceptance of the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon, with State Department concurrence for service determinations. Before the amendment the Coast Guard officer named was the Secretary of the Treasury; after section 68 of EO 13286 (effective March 1, 2003) it is the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the substance of the clause is otherwise unchanged. The clause continues as amended, was not revoked or superseded in any held source, and was operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
EO 11139 (Johnson, signed 1964-01-07, 29 FR 227, published 1964-01-09) authorizes the Secretary of Defense, for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps, and the Secretary of the Treasury, for Coast Guard members when the Coast Guard is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted, and requires the concurrence of the Secretary of State for determinations that service with the United Nations in a particular area or for a particular purpose is a justifiable basis. Section 68 of EO 13286 (signed 2003-02-28; its text is held as an American Presidency Project transcription, and its section 92 says the order becomes effective on March 1, 2003) amends it by striking the Secretary of the Treasury and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security. Under the owner strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The order has no own-terms end. The Federal Register disposition note lists only that amendment (EO 13286, February 28, 2003); the U.S. Code and eCFR bounded searches found no hit; a search of the held corpus for the order number finds only EO 13286, the 1989 codification and the order's own text. The order cites no statute, relying on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief, so no authority statute needs checking. This is a negative-search predicate.

savings.reason: The order is a continuing authorization with no end and no savings clause; the only later change found is the 2003 substitution of the Secretary of Homeland Security, which leaves the clause in force, so there is no residual beyond the operative clause itself.
